title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page sets up the classical picture. Take a projective line X over a field k of characteristic not 2, with a 4-element set I of marked points. The Klein four-group V = V(J) (identity and the three double transpositions of I) acts on X. The 6 fixed points of its three involutions form an 'octahedral' subset S, standard model {0, ∞, ±1, ±i}. The normalizer Γ = Nor_G(V) in G = Aut(X) = PGL2 is ≅ S4, sitting in an extension (*) 1 → V → Γ → Aut(V) ≅ S3 → 1.

This page:
(1) Splittings of (*) are the complements of V in S4. These are the four point-stabilizers S3 ⊂ S4, all conjugate. Geometrically they correspond to the four pairs of antipodal faces of the octahedron: the stabilizer in the rotation group of an antipodal pair of faces is a D3 ≅ S3 meeting V trivially.
(2) Combinatorial octahedron from (S, a). The data are the vertex set S and the antipodism a, a fixed-point-free involution with 3 orbits. The faces are the 3-subsets S' with S' ∪ a(S') = S, i.e. one vertex from each antipodal pair, giving 2^3 = 8 faces. The edges are the 2-subsets contained in a face.
(3) Γ is identified with the group of automorphisms of S preserving the octahedral structure together with an orientation ω. That is the rotation group S4, index 2 in Aut(S, a) ≅ S4 × Z/2 of order 48.
(4) Choosing the orientation amounts to choosing a square root of -1. In the standard model, the face {0,1,i} with its two cyclic orientations is used, and complex conjugation reverses orientation. Equivalently: given an oriented face (p, q, r), normalize p ↦ 0, a(p) ↦ ∞, q ↦ 1; then r goes to a well-defined square root of -1. So the 2-element torsor of orientations is canonically the set of primitive 4th roots of unity in k, compatibly with Galois action.
(5) Notation is introduced: Oct(V) ⊂ X is the octahedron, and I(V) = F/a is the set of antipodal face pairs, of cardinality 4. The next page states that Γ(V) acts on I(V), that Γ(V) ≅ S_{I(V)}, and that I(V) is naturally a V-torsor. It then gives the proposition: a bijection between Klein subgroups V ⊂ PGL2(k), S4-subgroups Γ, and octahedral 6-subsets S. The margin adds an equivalence of categories between pairs (X, V), (X, Γ), (X, S) and oriented combinatorial octahedra.

Purpose: an intrinsic, Galois-equivariant (torsor-style) description of the symmetry of M_{0,4}. This is a building block for the 'surgery of conformal surfaces' project, where octahedral and tetrahedral configurations on P^1 serve as gluing models.
errors: Not an error on this page, but relevant to the next page's proposition: over a general k, existence and conjugacy of Klein subgroups, and Nor_G(V) ≅ S4, need sqrt(-1) ∈ k. Over Q or R the normalizer of the standard V in PGL2(k) is only D4 of order 8, and non-split Klein subgroups can occur. Grothendieck's hypothesis 'stable under square roots' covers this.
The identification 'orientation ↔ sqrt(-1)' is canonical only after fixing a convention (which oriented face maps to +i). The torsor statement is correct; calling it a 'choice' is fine.
Minor: the splittings are 'identified with' face-pairs via the stabilizer. Distinct face pairs give distinct, conjugate complements, so the bijection with the 4 complements is correct.

ideas.what: Klein four-group V ⊂ PGL2 with normalizer S4; the octahedral 6-point configuration as the fixed points of V's involutions
ideas.where_published: Not as such. Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} and the Klein group in the Teichmüller tower only in passing.

ideas.what: Complements of V in S4 (four conjugate S3's) correspond to the four pairs of antipodal faces of the octahedron
ideas.modern_name: complements in the split extension V ⋊ S3 = S4

ideas.what: Combinatorial octahedron defined from a 6-set with a fixed-point-free involution: faces are the 3-subsets S' with S' ∪ a(S') = S
ideas.modern_name: cross-polytope / orthoplex as a simplicial complex (join of three S^0)

ideas.what: Orientations of the octahedral configuration in P^1(k) correspond canonically to square roots of -1 in k
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (implicit in descriptions of octahedral subgroups of PGL2 over non-closed fields, e.g. Beauville's 'Finite subgroups of PGL2(K)')

ideas.what: Set I(V) of antipodal face pairs as a V-torsor with Γ ≅ S_{I(V)}; categorical equivalence between (X, V), (X, S) and oriented octahedra
ideas.modern_name: torsor description of the S4-symmetry of M_{0,4}

missed.claim: A canonical, Galois-equivariant identification: orientations of the octahedral configuration in P^1(k) ↔ square roots of -1 in k. It is part of a functorial, field-independent treatment of the octahedral symmetry of M_{0,4}, intended as input for a 'surgery of conformal surfaces' (gluing along standard configurations). Mathematically classical, but this torsor-style packaging inside Grothendieck's surgery project is not documented.
missed.quote: Donc le choix d'une orientation revient au choix d'une racine carrée de -1.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of minor interest to historians of the Esquisse / dessins / Teichmüller-tower circle. It shows Grothendieck treating M_{0,4} with its S4 symmetry arithmetically, over arbitrary k, which ties to the Galois action on the genus-0 'building blocks' of the tower.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is Klein's classical octahedral picture (V ⊂ S4 ⊂ PGL2, complements ↔ antipodal face pairs, orientation ↔ i), recast in torsor/categorical language over a general field. It is correct and neat but routine for a specialist. Its interest is mainly historical: it documents the surgery project's elementary building blocks.
transcription_corrections: 'le sous-groupe de Γ qui l'invariant' should read 'le sous-groupe de Γ qui le laisse invariant'.
Below (*), the image reads 'Nor_G(V)' under Γ (with '‖') and '≃ 𝔖_3' under Aut(V).
'à priori' is 'a priori' in the manuscript.
'Pour un sous-groupe V ≃ [?]' is 'V ≃ 𝔻₂' (Klein group), matching the next page.
'I(V) = F/a_I' is better read as 'I(V) = F/a', the quotient of the face set by the antipodism.
In the lines on Γ, the margin insertion is '$F \subset \mathfrak{P}_3(S)$' and the edge set is '$A \subset \mathfrak{P}_2(S)$' (parts of cardinality 3 and 2), not 'F_3(S)', 'F_2(S)'.
